items.title: One Voice, Countless Worlds, Each Listener Understanding in Their Own Way

items.zh: 廣音具足者，謂佛菩薩所說化語，其聲廣大，隨其所樂，無量種類天、龍、藥叉、健達縛、阿素洛、揭路荼、緊捺洛、牟呼洛伽、聲聞、菩薩、人、非人等無量眾會，一踰繕那皆悉充滿，以妙圓音隨類遍告。又隨所樂，小千世界、二千世界、三千世界，乃至十方無量無數諸世界中，若近、若遠所有眾會，以妙圓音隨類遍告。於此聲中出種種音，為諸眾生說種種法，隨其所應，各得義利。
items.en: Vast in reach: conjured speech whose sound is vast, extending as far as wished ... proclaiming the teaching to every kind of being through its wondrous, perfect tone. ... Within this single sound, various specific teachings emerge, expounding various specific dharmas to various beings, each according to what benefits them, each attaining genuine benefit.

items.zh: 繫屬於自者，謂佛菩薩所說化語，於化自身出種種音，宣說正法，誨責放逸。繫屬於他者，謂佛菩薩所說化語，於化他身宣說正法，誨責放逸。無所繫屬者，謂佛菩薩所說化語，或於空中、或於所化非情法上而有所說。宣說正法言詞所攝者，謂佛菩薩所說化語，開示正理，令諸愚癡於種種法皆得悟解。誨責放逸言詞所攝者，謂佛菩薩所說化語，為不愚癡獲得淨信而放逸者，責其放逸，令生慚愧；誨不放逸，令勤修學。如是所說眾多化事略有三種，化身、化境，及以化語。當知如是一切能化神境智通品類差別，一一分別無量無數。

items.title: Section: Miraculous Ability Closes; Past-Life Recall Opens With Eight Recalled Details

items.zh: 如是二種諸佛菩薩神境智通能辦二事。一者、示現種種神通，引諸眾生入佛聖教。二者、示現種種神通，惠施無量受苦眾生眾多品類利益安樂。
items.en: These two kinds of miraculous ability accomplish two things for buddhas and bodhisattvas. First, displaying various miraculous powers draws beings into the Buddha's own teaching. Second, displaying various miraculous powers bestows many kinds of benefit and ease upon immeasurable suffering beings.

items.zh: 云何諸佛菩薩隨念宿住智通？
謂佛菩薩以宿住智，自能隨念己之宿住，曾於如是有情類中，我如是名，如經廣說。亦能隨念他諸有情身等一切品類差別，如自隨念己事無異。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas, through the wisdom of recalling past lives, are able to recall their own past existences — that among such and such a kind of being, they bore such and such a name — exactly as elaborated in the sūtras. ... They are likewise able to recall the same range of details for other beings, no differently than recalling their own affairs.

items.zh: 又能令他得宿住智，能自隨念前際所經若自、若他身等一切品類差別，曾於如是有情類中，我如是名，乃至廣說。如是有情轉復令他得宿住智，能自隨念一切宿住，如前無異。如是展轉令憶宿住，皆如自己。於現法中，又能隨念諸微細事，所有一切若少若多先所造作、先所思惟，皆無忘失。又能隨念無間剎那，次第所作無間斷故。又能隨念有量有數宿住差別，所知時劫可算數故。又能隨念無量無數宿住差別，所知時劫不可數故。以要言之，此宿住智於如是處、於如是類、於如是量，隨其所欲皆無礙轉。如是名為諸佛菩薩隨念宿住所攝威力。

items.title: Section: Why the Buddha Recalls Past Lives — The Nine-Coloured Deer and the Self-Sacrificing Rabbit

items.zh: 又由隨念宿住智故，憶念本生，為諸有情開示先世種種品類第一希有菩薩所行難行苦行。令於佛所生淨信故，起恭敬故，令於生死深厭離故。
items.en: Moreover, by means of the wisdom of recalling past lives, they recollect their own former births, revealing to beings the most extraordinary and difficult bodhisattva conduct undertaken in various past existences — so that pure faith arises towards the Buddha, so that reverence arises, and so that deep weariness with birth-and-death arises.

items.title: Recalling Past Lives Refutes the Wrong View of Permanence

items.zh: 又由此智憶念本事，為諸眾生開示種種先世相應業果異熟，為令妄計前際常論、一分常論常見眾生破常見故。
items.en: Moreover, by means of this wisdom, they recollect the past-life stories of disciples and others, revealing to beings the various ripened karmic fruits corresponding to former lives — in order to break the wrong view of those who mistakenly hold to eternalism regarding the past, whether wholesale or partial eternalism.

items.zh: 云何諸佛菩薩天耳智通？

blocks.text: The power of the Buddha's voice, then the recollection of past lives and why it is used. Two short passages (0493b29, 0493c21) are untranslated. The first explains conjured speech that comes from one's own conjured body, from another's, or from empty space and inanimate things, used to teach the Dharma and to rebuke heedlessness.

Conjured speech is "vast in reach, extending as far as wished". "Within this single sound, various specific teachings emerge, each according to what benefits the listener." This is the classical idea that the Buddha speaks with one voice and each being understands in their own way.
Two reasons: "to draw beings into the Buddha's teaching", and to inspire faith and respect. Venerable Miào Jìng: entering the teaching still requires practice; the display only opens the door.

"Through the wisdom of recalling past lives, they recall their own past existences: among such a kind of being, they bore such a name", and so on, "as in the sūtras". The untranslated prose (0493c21) adds: they can give others the same recollection, who can give it to others in turn; they recall "subtle matters, everything done or thought before, without loss"; moment after moment without gap; past aeons countable and uncountable.

To reveal "the most extraordinary and difficult bodhisattva conduct undertaken in past existences", so that beings are inspired. The birth stories (jātaka) come from this. And recalling the past lives of disciples "breaks the wrong view of those who hold to eternalism": seeing how beings change from life to life, one cannot believe in a permanent self.

quiz.q: "Within this single sound, various teachings emerge … each attaining benefit." What verse does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: "The Buddha speaks with one voice; beings each understand by their kind"
"all conditioned things are like a dream"
"if one wishes to know all buddhas"
quiz.why: "Within this single sound, various specific teachings emerge, expounding various specific dharmas to various beings, each according to what benefits them." Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Buddha speaks the Dharma with one voice; beings each understand by their kind; all think the Tathāgata speaks their language, teaching them alone."

quiz.q: Miraculous ability "draws beings into the Buddha's teaching." What is needed to enter, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: "First, displaying various miraculous powers draws beings into the Buddha's own teaching." Venerable Miào Jìng: "entering the Buddha's teaching" requires faith.

quiz.q: Recalling past births reveals "difficult bodhisattva conduct." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: seeing a starving tigress, offering his own body — perfecting giving
quiz.why: "They recollect their own former births, revealing to beings the most extraordinary and difficult bodhisattva conduct undertaken in various past existences." Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing a starving tiger, offering his own body to feed it, perfecting the perfection of giving — these are jātaka stories.

quiz.q: "Recollecting 本事 … to break eternalism" — rendered "past events." What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: beyond jātakas, accounts of disciples' and others' past lives; Miào Jìng: eternalism wrongly holds the past unchanging
quiz.why: "By means of this wisdom, they recollect past events, revealing … in order to break the wrong view of those who mistakenly hold to eternalism." Master Cháng Bǎi: besides jātakas about the Buddha's past lives, accounts the Buddha gives of disciples' and others' past lives are 本事. Venerable Miào Jìng: eternalism wrongly holds that the past is unchanging, permanent.
